title: AB 2047's Clock Starts Ticking, Laser Z-Layers Go Public & UV-Printed Puzzles
subtitle: This week in 3D printing news

topics.title: AB 2047: The Clock Is Running
topics.description: Formally presented to Newsom Monday — now he has to act

slides.heading: AB 2047: The Decision Clock Starts
slides.body: Two weeks ago we covered the legislature passing this bill. Monday, September 14, the formal step happened: enrolled and presented to Governor Newsom at 1:30 p.m. That starts his decision clock — sign it, veto it, or it becomes law without his signature. California has no pocket veto.
bullets: Enrolled and presented September 14 — he must act by September 30
What's on his desk: consumer printers sold in California must eventually ship with 'firearm blocking technology'
The stripped-down version — the Senate removed the most aggressive enforcement tools before the August 31 floor votes
Everytown and Moms Demand Action are pushing hard for a signature; Prusa, VORON, EFF and the maker community remain opposed
Our regulation tracker gets updated the day he moves

topics.title: Toolchanger Watch: Creality Steps In
topics.description: The K3 nozzle-changer gets real at IFA — and the rest of the field checks in

slides.heading: Creality K3: The Nozzle-Changer Goes Official
slides.body: Remember KliTek from back in May? It's real now: Creality put the K3 product page live at IFA Berlin on September 4 and picked up an IFA Innovation Award for it. Not a full toolchanger — it swaps NOZZLES, not toolheads — but it's Creality's answer to the multi-tool year.
bullets: K3 is the new K-series flagship: CoreXY with the KliTek automatic nozzle-changing system
Nozzle swaps, not toolhead swaps — under 5 seconds a change, per Creality's page
Release window is Q3 2026 — which ends in two weeks
The rest of the field: INDX quiet this week (PrusaSlicer 3.0 still owes the Config Wizard profiles), Sovol M1D pre-orders running, Co Print's Quadro Kickstarter due in October

topics.title: Follow-Ups: Pre-Order Day Delivered
topics.description: Three stories from past weeks all hit their dates

slides.heading: September 15 Was Follow-Up Day
slides.body: Three running stories hit their marks this week — and every number came in at or under what we reported.
bullets: SUNLU FilaDC i10: pre-order is LIVE at $179.99 — beats the 'under $200' rumor from last week's slide; ships from December
FibreSeeker 3: US webstore open, $3,199 early bird (from $3,499), capped at 500 units through September 30
HeyGears G1X: the Kickstarter closed September 11 at $17,463,066 from 3,927 backers — 17,463% funded; late pledges are open
My advice on all three hasn't changed: let the first wave take the pre-order risk

topics.title: Maker's Muse: UV Printing on Print-in-Place Puzzles
topics.description: Full-color art on a sliding puzzle, straight off the printer

slides.heading: UV Art on a Print-in-Place Puzzle
slides.body: Angus at Maker's Muse combined two things we've covered separately: a parametric print-in-place sliding puzzle, then a UV flatbed printer putting full-color artwork straight onto the tiles. We talked UV printers when the HeyGears campaign ran — this is what the tech looks like in a maker's hands.

slides.heading: Why It Works So Well
bullets: The puzzle prints assembled — tiles never leave the frame, so the printed image stays registered
Flat color looks good; the textured RELIEF print with real tactile depth is the showstopper
Hackaday picked it up September 16 — expect a wave of UV-decorated print-in-place designs
UV flatbeds are the crossover tool of the year: 2D printing that understands 3D objects

topics.title: Throw It at the Printer: VR Meets the Print Queue
topics.description: A Quest 3 workflow where hurling a model across the room starts the print

slides.heading: Model It in VR, Throw It, It Prints
slides.body: The fun one this week: a software engineer wired a Meta Quest 3 to his Bambu P2S so he can grab a 3D model in VR and physically THROW it across the room at the printer — and the print starts. His words: 'I've never felt more like Tony Stark.'
bullets: The glue is simple: a local webserver on his PC connects the headset, the phone app, and the printer
He vibe-coded the pipeline with AI assistance rather than writing it by hand
Code isn't public yet — he says he'll release it if there's enough interest, so go make interest
Silly demo, serious point: printer APIs are now open enough that one person can build this

topics.title: Robotics Corner: A 3D-Printed Boat Doing 40 Knots
topics.description: UMaine's 3Dirigo X — large-format printing at 500 pounds an hour

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: 3Dirigo X Hits the Water
slides.body: Our large-format beat delivered a boat. UMaine's Advanced Structures and Composites Center christened the 3Dirigo X in Hampden, Maine — a 30-foot 3D-printed vessel engineered for offshore conditions at speeds approaching 40 knots. It's back in this week's news as the trials story spreads.
bullets: Successor to 2019's 3Dirigo, the proof-of-concept that took three Guinness World Records
The number that matters: print rate went from 20 pounds an hour in 2019 to 500 pounds an hour now
3D-printed composites, designed for real open-ocean forces — not a demo hull
Funded through the federal Accelerated Rapid Prototyping initiative; targets include commercial boatbuilding, unmanned vessels, and patrol craft
Same trend line as our robot-arm segment: large-format printing is leaving the lab at industrial speed

topics.title: Builder Spotlight: Laser Z-Layers, Released
topics.description: The laser-welded layer build from W34 is now a repo you can build

slides.heading: Builder Spotlight: 'I Changed a Thing' Releases the Laser Mod
slides.body: Back in August we covered the build that welds each layer to the last with toolhead lasers — Z-strength hitting 94% of X in ABS. This week the builder released the whole project: a GitHub repo so you can put lasers on your own printer. And yes — I'll say it again — this was my idea years ago.

slides.heading: What's in the Repo
bullets: CAD files and drawings for the laser mod kit, built around a modified Elegoo Neptune 4
Klipper config with the laser PWM wiring, plus OrcaSlicer post-processing scripts that inject the laser commands
An offline web portal: G-code visualizer, toolhead simulator, calibration tools — zero setup
Experimental and at-your-own-risk: laser safety glasses and ventilation are mandatory, and some smoothing modes still have bugs

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Tinkercad exports are smarter than you think

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Don't Group Before You Export
slides.body: Tinkercad changed how export works, and most people never noticed: leave your shapes UNGROUPED and they stay separate objects in the exported file — which unlocks real slicer tricks.
bullets: Export OBJ with shapes ungrouped and Bambu Studio lets you assign a different filament color to each shape
Separate shapes can also act as slicer MODIFIERS — overlap a box and bump just that zone to 80% infill
Slicers handle the intersections: no extra internal walls where separate shapes overlap
One exception: if the design contains a hole shape, Tinkercad still groups everything on export — cut your holes, then export
